title: Physical activity and your heart health
paragraphs: Regular physical activity is one of the best things you can do for your heart health. Increasing your physical activity from as little as 10 minutes a day to the Australian Government’s recommended 30 to 45 minutes a day, five or more days of the week can help reduce your risk of heart disease and heart attacks. It can also prevent and manage many conditions and diseases, including some cancers, type 2 diabetes and depression.

Building up your physical activity to the recommended level has many benefits. By making your heart work a little harder, you can cut your risk of heart disease by a third – regardless of your age, gender, income or where you live.

Our busy, often sedentary lifestyle makes it hard to do the recommended amount of physical activity. But it’s good to know you are never too old or too young to move more.This diagram illustrates how much activity is advised by Australian Government guidelines for better health based on your age group.Moderate-intensity exercise– Activities that make your heart beat faster but don’t make you breathless.Vigorous-intensity exercise– High-intensity activities that make your heart rate higher and breathe more heavily.For more on the recommendations,visit Australia's Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines and the Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines.
Nine out of 10 Australians could reduce the risk of heart disease by walking as little as 15 minutes more each day.
Physical activity and exercise can do wonders for your physical and mental health.
